title-group.article-title: Paired-biopsy analysis of PD-L1 expression before and after anti-PD-1 therapy in metastatic melanoma.

contrib-group.aff: Harborview Institute of Oncology, San Diego, CA
Midland Academic Medical Center, Columbus, OH
Eastgate Cancer Research Network, New York, NY

permissions.copyright-statement: © 2026 by American Society of Clinical Oncology

abstract.p: Background: Acquired resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in metastatic melanoma may involve dynamic changes in therapeutic targets and associated signaling pathways. We evaluated longitudinal changes in PD-L1 using paired tumor samples collected before treatment and at disease progression. Methods: Institutional databases were queried to identify patients with metastatic melanoma who received anti-PD-1 therapy and had paired pretreatment and post-progression biopsies. Samples were assessed by multiplex immunofluorescence and RNA expression profiling. Marker abundance was compared within patients, and associations with clinical outcomes were explored using nonparametric tests. Results: Paired samples from 29 patients passed quality control. Median progression-free survival on therapy was 7.1 months. Baseline PD-L1 expression was 18% positive tumor cells, with a median on-treatment change of +11 percentage points. Substantial loss of PD-L1 was observed in 8 patients, whereas the remaining samples showed stable or increased expression. Ifng signature changed by +22% across paired samples (p=0.04). The aggregate pattern was consistent with divergent immune adaptation across responding and resistant lesions. Conclusions: Longitudinal changes in PD-L1 after anti-PD-1 therapy were heterogeneous in metastatic melanoma. Resistance was not explained by a single uniform biomarker shift, supporting multi-analyte assessment of paired samples and further mechanistic study. Research Sponsor: None.
